title: Senate Committee Hearing
subtitle: Senate HELP Committee — Insulin Pricing and Affordability

sources.name: JAMA — Insulin Pricing in the United States (2025)

metadata.laymanSummary: Senate HELP Committee heard testimony from diabetes patients, doctors, and pharmaceutical executives about why insulin prices remain unaffordable for millions of Americans.

data.billTitle: Hearing: Why Do Americans Pay 10x More for Insulin Than Canadians?

speakers.name: Sen. Bernie Sanders
speakers.title: I-VT · HELP Committee Chair
speakers.quote: Novo Nordisk charges $300 for a vial of insulin in America. The same product in Canada: $30. In Germany: $9. The CEO of Novo Nordisk is in this room. I would like him to explain to the millions of Americans who ration insulin how that pricing is justified.

speakers.name: Sen. Ted Cruz
speakers.title: R-TX · Senate Commerce
speakers.quote: This is an issue that cuts across party lines. Texans with Type 1 diabetes are rationing insulin and dying. I don't care which party solves this problem — I want it solved. Every option should be on the table, including greater transparency and real competition.

speakers.name: Sen. Jack Reed
speakers.title: D-RI · Senate Armed Services
speakers.quote: We have testimony today from a nurse in Rhode Island who has watched three patients die from insulin rationing in the past year. Not in a developing country. In the richest nation in the history of the world. The committee will not leave this hearing without a plan.

data.title: About This Hearing
data.text: The Senate HELP Committee heard testimony on May 10, 2026 from pharmaceutical executives, endocrinologists, and diabetes patients including a diabetic teenager who detailed nearly dying after rationing insulin at $18/hour minimum wage. Senators from both parties expressed urgency. The hearing set the stage for floor votes on insulin price caps and Medicare negotiation bills.

data.title: Should the government cap the price of insulin?

options.label: Yes — no one should die over insulin costs
Increase competition instead of price caps
